info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance — Unit 4 (Simulation Day): morning base-check start. Rich item bank split by skill: Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

name.text: U04-L1 Dialogue 1 how many task cards

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again (reading the work pack). How many task cards does the work pack contain?

generalfeedback.text: Mechanic A says there are six task cards, each a separate job with its own sign-off box.

feedback.text: Correct — six separate task cards.
No — listen again to the count A gives.
No — the pack holds fewer than eight.
No — that is too many; check the number A states.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again (opening the panels). How many panel fasteners are on access panel 191AB? Write the number in figures.

generalfeedback.text: Mechanic A counts twenty fasteners and bags them so none becomes FOD.

feedback.text: Correct — twenty fasteners.
Not quite — A counts twenty fasteners on the panel.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again (reporting the defect). About how long is the crack, in millimetres? Write the number in figures.

generalfeedback.text: Mechanic A says the crack measures about twelve millimetres and photographs it beside a ruler.

feedback.text: Correct — about twelve millimetres.
Not quite — the crack is about twelve millimetres.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. True or false: the nose is jacked before the wings.

generalfeedback.text: False. The AMM instructs the wings first and the nose last.

feedback.text: No — the order is wings first, nose last.
Correct — the nose is jacked last, after the wings.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. True or false: the mechanics measure the crack before they call the supervisor.

generalfeedback.text: True. They measure first, so they can give the supervisor an accurate number.

feedback.text: Correct — measure first, then call.
No — they measure the crack before calling.

name.text: U04-L6 what comes first in the plan

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. In the pair's agreed plan, what comes first?

generalfeedback.text: Documentation first, aircraft second: they review the paperwork before they touch the aircraft.

feedback.text: Correct — documentation first, aircraft second.
No — that comes after the paperwork is reviewed.
No — the panel is opened much later in the sequence.
No — inspection is one of the last steps.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again (the night-shift voicemail). What does Marek ask the day shift to do first?

generalfeedback.text: He asks them to review the tech log first, then divide the task cards.

feedback.text: Correct — review the tech log first.
No — the work order is already open and authorised.
No — the cordon is already established; only verify it.
No — that comes after reading the tech log.

questiontext.text:
Read this text, then answer.

A Minimum Equipment List (MEL) lets an aircraft be dispatched with certain items inoperative for a limited time, if set conditions are met. Each MEL item has a rectification interval, for example three days for a Category C item.

What does an MEL allow?

generalfeedback.text: An MEL permits dispatch with some items inoperative, but only for a limited time and under stated conditions.

feedback.text: Correct — limited time, set conditions.
No — the relief is time-limited, not permanent.

answer.text: Dispatch with no conditions at all.

feedback.text: No — conditions must be met.
No — an MEL is about dispatch, not repair.

questiontext.text:
Read this text, then answer.

A Service Bulletin (SB) is issued by the manufacturer to recommend an inspection or a modification. Unless an Airworthiness Directive makes it mandatory, an SB is normally advisory.

True or false: a Service Bulletin is always mandatory.

generalfeedback.text: False. An SB is normally advisory unless an Airworthiness Directive makes it mandatory.

feedback.text: No — an SB is advisory unless an AD makes it mandatory.
Correct — normally advisory, not always mandatory.

questiontext.text:
Read this text, then answer.

An Airworthiness Directive (AD) is issued by the aviation authority. Compliance is mandatory, and it must be completed by a stated deadline.

Who issues an Airworthiness Directive?

generalfeedback.text: The aviation authority issues ADs, and compliance is mandatory by the deadline.

feedback.text: Correct — the authority issues the AD.
No — the mechanic complies with it, but does not issue it.
No — the crew do not issue ADs.
No — the supplier does not issue ADs.

questiontext.text:
Read this text, then answer.

A BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) readout lists fault codes stored by an aircraft system. The technician reads a code, then finds its meaning in the AMM fault table.

Where does the technician find the meaning of a BITE fault code?

generalfeedback.text: The code is looked up in the AMM fault table, which explains what each code means.

feedback.text: Correct — the AMM fault table explains the code.
No — the IPC lists parts, not fault codes.
No — the tech log records defects, not code meanings.
No — the label is not a fault-code source.

name.text: U04-R5 purpose of a work order

questiontext.text:
Read this text, then answer.

A work order in a work pack is the legal authority to start a maintenance job. It is opened and authorised before any work, and it is signed off only when the job is complete.

A work order in a work pack mainly provides...

generalfeedback.text: The work order is the legal authority to begin; part numbers, torque values and crack limits come from other documents.

feedback.text: Correct — it authorises the job to begin.

answer.text: the part numbers for the job.

feedback.text: No — part numbers come from the IPC.
No — torque values come from the AMM.

answer.text: the crack limits for a bracket.

feedback.text: No — limits (if any) are in the AMM.

questiontext.text:
Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb remove:

After ______ the panel, log the torque.

generalfeedback.text: After before and after, use the -ing form: after removing. Latvian and Russian have no gerund, so the -ing is often dropped.

feedback.text: Correct — after + -ing.
Use the -ing form after "after": removing.
The answer is "removing" (after + -ing).

questiontext.text:
Correct the sequencer for step one. Write the correct single word:

______ , set up the safety cordon. (not "At first")

generalfeedback.text: For step one, use First. "At first" means "in the beginning, but it later changed" — a common carry-over from sākumā / сначала.

feedback.text: Correct — "First," for step one.
No — "at first" is for something that later changed. Use "First".
The answer is "First".

questiontext.text:
Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb jack:

Before ______ the aircraft, set the chocks.

generalfeedback.text: After before, use the -ing form: before jacking.

feedback.text: Correct — before + -ing.
Use the -ing form after "before": jacking.
The answer is "jacking".

questiontext.text:
Add the missing connector (three words) that means "immediately after":

______ the aircraft is up, we fit the lockout pins.

generalfeedback.text: The three-word connector is as soon as. ("Once" also works, but it is one word.)

feedback.text: Correct — "as soon as" (three words).
Also accepted — "once" carries the same meaning.
Incomplete — the full connector is "as soon as".
The answer is "as soon as".

questiontext.text: Which document (two words) authorises the mechanics to begin work?

generalfeedback.text: The work order is the legal authority to start. Nothing begins until it is open and signed.

feedback.text: Correct — the work order.
No — the work pack is the whole set of paperwork; the work order authorises the job.
The answer is "work order".

questiontext.text: Loose items on the hangar floor that can damage an engine or a tyre are called ______ (a three-letter abbreviation).

generalfeedback.text: FOD = foreign object debris. A misplaced fastener becomes FOD, so fasteners are bagged.

feedback.text: Correct — FOD (foreign object debris).
Close in meaning, but the required abbreviation is FOD.
The answer is "FOD".

questiontext.text:
Add the missing article (one word):

First, jack ______ aircraft, then remove the wheel.

generalfeedback.text: English needs the article: jack the aircraft. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so "the" is easily dropped.

feedback.text: Correct — "jack the aircraft".
No — the aircraft is a specific one, so use "the".
The answer is "the".

questiontext.text: Match each hangar-workflow term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: work order = authority to begin; task card = one job; tech log = record of defects; sign-off = certifying signature; defect = a fault found.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are correct — check the rest against the vocabulary bank.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: The document that authorises work to begin
One job, with its own steps and sign-off box
The record of defects and completed work
The certifying signature that a job is complete
A fault or damage found on the aircraft

name.text: U04-V2 term to meaning B safety

questiontext.text: Match each safety term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: safety cordon = a barrier keeping people out; wheel chock = a wedge against a tyre; lockout = pins stopping a jack lowering; jack point = the fixed spot for a jack pad; warning notice = a sign not to enter.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are correct — check the rest against the vocabulary bank.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the vocabulary bank and try again.

answer.text: A barrier that keeps people out of the area
A wedge placed against a tyre
Pins that stop a jack lowering unexpectedly
The fixed spot where a jack pad must sit
A displayed sign not to enter or operate

questiontext.text: Match each abbreviation to its full name.

generalfeedback.text: AMM = Aircraft Maintenance Manual; IPC = Illustrated Parts Catalogue; MEL = Minimum Equipment List; AD = Airworthiness Directive; FOD = foreign object debris.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are correct — check the rest.

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb it goes with (its natural collocation).

generalfeedback.text: Natural partners: raise a work order; record the torque; set up a safety cordon; open the access panel; check for FOD.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Some pairs are correct — check the collocations again.

incorrectfeedback.text: Review the collocations in the vocabulary bank.
